positioning: research prototype / working proof of concept / finalist demonstration prototype

claims.claim: The frozen final benchmark contains 1,200 procedurally generated synthetic journeys.
claims.evidence: Archived final summary and manifest: n_cases 1200, seed 20261123, generator mgen-1.0, dataset SHA-256 28a3979e...8697.
claims.evidence_scope: Synthetic journeys produced by a seeded procedural generator; ground truth comes from an independent oracle over a latent world, not from the engine.
allowed_wording: The frozen final benchmark has 1,200 procedurally generated synthetic journeys.
1,200 frozen synthetic journeys.
claims.limitations: Synthetic data only; no real passengers, cameras or checkpoint operations are involved.

claims.claim: On the frozen 1,200-journey synthetic benchmark the full dual-channel system achieved 95.0% exact violation-set accuracy.
claims.evidence: Archived system_comparison.csv full_dual_channel exact_set_accuracy = 0.95 (95% bootstrap CI 0.9375-0.9625).
claims.evidence_scope: Frozen synthetic benchmark only. Exact match means the predicted violation-label set equals the oracle set; supersets or subsets do not match.
allowed_wording: On a frozen 1,200-journey synthetic benchmark, the full dual-channel system achieved 95.0% exact violation-set accuracy.
95.0% exact violation-set accuracy (frozen synthetic benchmark).
claims.limitations: Not a camera, field or real-world accuracy. The 5.0% of non-matching journeys are the 60 weak-physical-evidence cases (see C009).

claims.claim: On the frozen synthetic benchmark the full dual-channel system achieved a Macro-F1 of 0.981 (95% bootstrap CI 0.976-0.986).
claims.evidence: Archived macro_f1 0.981156; percentile bootstrap CI [0.976081, 0.985872] (2000 resamples, seed 20261017).
claims.evidence_scope: Frozen synthetic benchmark; Macro-F1 is the mean of per-violation-type F1 over the four violation types. The CI is a statistical interval over this synthetic sample, not a field interval.
allowed_wording: Macro-F1 of 0.981 [95% bootstrap CI 0.976-0.986] on the frozen synthetic benchmark.
0.981 Macro-F1 (frozen synthetic benchmark).
claims.limitations: Macro-F1 is an F1 score, not accuracy. Synthetic benchmark only.

claims.evidence_scope: Frozen synthetic benchmark; micro-averaged over all TYPE:STEP labels.
allowed_wording: Micro-F1 of 0.973 on the frozen synthetic benchmark.
claims.limitations: F1 score, not accuracy; synthetic benchmark only.

claims.claim: On the frozen synthetic benchmark the full dual-channel system raised an alarm for every one of the 812 violated journeys (0 of 812 without an alarm).
claims.evidence: Archived violated_missed_entirely 0, violated_cases 812, fnr_violated 0.0 for full_dual_channel.
claims.evidence_scope: Frozen synthetic benchmark. 'Alarm' means at least one violation label was raised on a journey whose oracle status is VIOLATED.
allowed_wording: The full dual-channel system flagged all 812 violated journeys in the frozen synthetic benchmark (0 of 812 without an alarm).
0 / 812 violated journeys without an alarm.
prohibited_wording: 100% of real security violations are detected
claims.limitations: Says nothing about real violations. The same system also raised 60 false phantom-completion alarms on violation-free journeys (C009).

claims.claim: On the frozen synthetic benchmark, phantom completion detection had recall 1.000 and precision 0.860 (F1 0.925).
claims.evidence: Archived per-class row PHANTOM_COMPLETION: truth 368, tp 368, fp 60, fn 0, precision 0.859813, recall 1.0, F1 0.924623.
claims.evidence_scope: Frozen synthetic benchmark. The 60 false positives are the weak-physical-evidence cases described in C009.
allowed_wording: On the frozen synthetic benchmark, phantom completion recall was 1.000 and precision 0.860 (F1 0.925).
claims.limitations: Precision is below 1 because of 60 false alarms; do not describe this class as perfect.

claims.claim: Within the frozen synthetic benchmark, channel contradiction detection had precision, recall and F1 of 1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000.
claims.evidence: Archived per-class row CHANNEL_CONTRADICTION: truth 240, tp 240, fp 0, fn 0.
claims.evidence_scope: Frozen synthetic benchmark only; scope must always be stated alongside the figure.
allowed_wording: Within the frozen synthetic benchmark, channel contradiction was detected with precision, recall and F1 of 1.000.
claims.limitations: Generated contradiction patterns are clean by construction; real inconsistency patterns may differ.

claims.claim: Cross-channel reasoning enabled detection of phantom completion and channel contradiction that the single-channel ablations and the simple procedure check did not identify.
claims.evidence: Archived per-class rows: physical-only, digital-only and simple-check have recall 0.0 for PHANTOM_COMPLETION (368 missed) and CHANNEL_CONTRADICTION (240 missed); the full system has recall 1.0 for both.
claims.evidence_scope: Frozen synthetic benchmark. Physical-only and digital-only are INTERNAL ABLATIONS of the same engine, not products or competitors. The simple check is a documented rule-based baseline written for this evaluation.
allowed_wording: In the frozen synthetic benchmark, only the dual-channel configuration detected phantom completion and channel contradiction; the internal single-channel ablations and the simple check did not.
Internal ablations show the value of cross-channel reasoning.
claims.limitations: No external or commercial system was evaluated. Those two violation types are definitionally cross-channel, so single-channel systems cannot detect them by design.

claims.claim: The primary known benchmark limitation is weak physical evidence: 60 low-confidence cases produced false phantom-completion alerts.
claims.evidence: Archived PHANTOM_COMPLETION fp = 60; family weak_physical_midjourney: 60 cases, 0 exact matches, 60 false-positive labels. The engine treats a sub-threshold physical observation as absent and raises PHANTOM_COMPLETION where the oracle expects UNCERTAIN. fpr_violation_free 0.154639 (60/388).
claims.evidence_scope: Frozen synthetic benchmark. Disclosed after the development run; no engine or oracle change was made.
allowed_wording: The primary known benchmark limitation is weak physical evidence: 60 low-confidence cases produced false phantom-completion alerts.
This reflects conservative evidence handling and has not been validated as an operationally optimal policy.
claims.limitations: Reflects conservative evidence handling; not validated as an operationally optimal policy. Future work: a calibrated treatment of sub-threshold physical evidence.
required_text: not been validated as an operationally optimal policy

claims.claim: The current prototype can convert live camera observations into temporary physical procedure events.
claims.evidence: M1 live pipeline (person detector, tracker, zone logic, event emitter) demonstrated on a webcam; unit tests cover zone and event logic without a camera.
claims.evidence_scope: Live demonstration of the pipeline. No accuracy, latency or field figure is claimed for it.
allowed_wording: The prototype converts live camera observations into temporary physical procedure events.
claims.limitations: No camera accuracy has been measured. The 95.0% figure is NOT a vision metric.

claims.claim: The prototype demonstrates live physical evidence combined with a SIMULATED DIGITAL CHANNEL.
claims.evidence: M2 dual-channel coordinator with a local digital event simulator (metadata source m2_digital_simulator, simulated true); shown on the M3 dashboard as SIMULATED DIGITAL CHANNEL.
claims.evidence_scope: Demonstration of cross-channel logic with a local simulator.
allowed_wording: Live physical evidence combined with a SIMULATED DIGITAL CHANNEL.
The digital channel is a local simulator.
prohibited_wording: connected to a live checkpoint system
claims.limitations: No integration with any real checkpoint, credential or border system exists.

claims.claim: The current prototype uses temporary journey tracking and does not require face recognition or persistent identity.
claims.evidence: Design and code: only a temporary tracker ID and a random journey UUID held in memory; no face detection, embeddings or identity fields; frames are processed in memory.
claims.evidence_scope: Current prototype design. This is a design property, not a certified privacy or security guarantee.
allowed_wording: The prototype uses temporary journey tracking and does not require face recognition or persistent identity.
claims.limitations: No formal privacy assessment has been performed. Deployment would need its own privacy and legal review.

claims.claim: Deterministic engine evaluation required tens of microseconds per case in the recorded benchmark environment (ENGINE EVALUATION ONLY).
claims.evidence: Archived final report latency table, full system: median 23.5 us, P95 48.5 us, P99 69.5 us over 6000 samples, measured in a sandbox (Python 3.12, Intel i7-10750H, 2 CPUs).
claims.evidence_scope: ENGINE EVALUATION ONLY: evidence already present as domain events. Excludes camera capture, YOLO inference, tracking, UI rendering and any external-system latency. Environment-specific.
allowed_wording: ENGINE EVALUATION ONLY: deterministic engine evaluation required tens of microseconds per case in the recorded benchmark environment.
claims.limitations: Measured once in a sandbox. Not a system, camera or end-to-end figure.

claims.claim: The frozen final split reproduced the development benchmark's overall full-system metrics closely.
claims.evidence: Development run (300 journeys, seed 20261017): exact-set accuracy 0.950, Macro-F1 0.981156, Micro-F1 0.973262, PHANTOM_COMPLETION precision 0.859813. Final run: 0.950, 0.981156, 0.973262, 0.859813. Dev point estimates are from the local, regenerable dev run (not archived in docs/).
claims.evidence_scope: The final split is independently seeded but is generated from the same procedural distribution and composition design as the development split. It is a frozen held-out synthetic benchmark, not an out-of-distribution or real-world validation set.
claims.verification_type: archived frozen result and descriptive comparison
allowed_wording: The frozen final split, independently seeded but generated from the same procedural distribution and composition design, reproduced the development benchmark's overall full-system metrics closely.
claims.limitations: Descriptive comparison only; no significance test was run. Agreement is expected because both splits share a generator design.
